title: A systolic murmur with syndromic clues / Screen for cardiomyopathy

blocks.text: A systolic murmur with syndromic clues / Screen for cardiomyopathy

AMaC MRCP PACES · R5-113 · Physical examination · PACES Station 3, cardiovascular · Skills A, B, D, E, G · 10 minutes (up to 6 examination, at least 4 questions) · Guideline dates and links in section 15 · Related AMaC: condition may appear elsewhere in a different context.
A young adult with short stature and a childhood heart murmur attends review. Examine the cardiovascular system to establish a cause.

sections.heading: 4. The Hook and the Examiner Trap

blocks.text:
HOOK — Pulmonary valve stenosis associated with Noonan syndrome can account for an ejection murmur and RV heave; also check for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
EXAMINER TRAP — Do not describe the murmur as aortic stenosis purely because it is ejection systolic.

RELEASED FINDINGS — on inspection, pulse, precordial palpation and auscultation as appropriate: Short stature, webbed neck, broad chest, right ventricular heave, ejection systolic murmur at upper left sternal edge radiating toward back, ejection click; no cyanosis or oedema.
Question 1 [R4] — Why left upper sternal murmur? | Right ventricular outflow/pulmonary valve obstruction.
Question 2 [R5] — What other heart problem? | Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
Question 3 [R6] — How confirm? | Echo and ECG, then genetics with counselling.
Question 4 [R7] — Other associations? | Variable growth, lymphatic and bleeding abnormalities.
Curveball — If a candidate asks for definitive proof from examination alone: “Explain what examination suggests and which confirmatory tests you need.”

Pulmonary valve stenosis associated with Noonan syndrome can account for an ejection murmur and RV heave; also check for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Do not describe the murmur as aortic stenosis purely because it is ejection systolic. Right ventricular outflow/pulmonary valve obstruction. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Echo and ECG, then genetics with counselling.

THINK: Noonan syndrome with pulmonary stenosis.
SAY: Pulmonary valve stenosis associated with Noonan syndrome can account for an ejection murmur and RV heave; also check for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
DO: Consent, focused cardiovascular examination, present findings and next tests.
NUMBERS: 10-minute examination encounter (PACES23).
TRAP: Do not describe the murmur as aortic stenosis purely because it is ejection systolic.
FINISH: Explain definitive investigations and appropriate specialist follow-up.
